note: Read 2026-11-04 by the research of a series and a play in every market (scratchpad l4t: the first wave t1-t8 and the follow-up u1-u25, merged item by item, the later verdict standing where it read more): what a series' and a play's producer can draw on there. sources.title: Federal Register of Legislation: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997, Volume 7 (Division 376), compilation as at 1 October 2026
sources.said: 376 ‑ 60 Amount of the producer offset The amount of the producer offset is: (a) if the * film is a * feature film that was produced for commercial exhibition to the public in cinemas—40%; or (b) otherwise—30%; of the total of the company’s * qualifying Australian production expenditure on the film … (b) the film is: (i) a * feature film or a film of a like nature; or (ii) a mini ‑ series of television drama; or (iii) a television series that is not covered by subparagraph (i) or (ii); and (c) the film is not, or is not to a substantial extent: … (ii) a film for exhibition as an advertising program or a commercial; or (iii) a film for exhibition as a discussion program, a quiz program, game show, a panel prog … (5) … (i) the series is made up of at least 2 episodes; and (ii) each episode of the series is at least one half of a commercial hour in duration, except where the film is predominantly made using cell, stop motion, digital or other animation, in which case each episode is at least one quarter of a commercial hour in duration … 5 A * film where the application for the certificate is for a series and not for a season of that series, and the series is not a * documentary $1 million $500,000 … 7 A * film where the application for the certificate is for a season of a series, and the series is not a * documentary $1 million $500,000 … (7) The amount worked out for a * film under this subsection is the amount worked out using the formula: where: duration of film in hours means the total length of the * film, measured in hours. total QAPE means the total of the company’s * qualifying Australian production expenditure on the * film … (ii) remuneration provided to the principal director, producers and principal cast associated with the film; to the extent that such expenditure comprises greater than 20% of the company’s * total film expenditure on the film; (c) for a series other than a drama series, or a season of a series other than a drama series—expenditure on an episode beyond the episode in which the 65th commercial hour of the series is reached.

sources.title: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997, compilation 268 (1 October 2026), volume 10, s 960-505
sources.said: 960 ‑ 505 Meaning of Australia Territories (1) Australia , when used in a geographical sense, includes each of the following: (a) Norfolk Island; (b) the Coral Sea Islands Territory; (c) the Territory of Ashmore and Cartier Islands; (d) the Territory of Christmas Island; (e) the Territory of Cocos (Keeling) Islands; (f) the Territory of Heard Island and the McDonald Islands.

figures.finding: Follows Australia: Australia's series and stage terms, as Australia's research holds them, would apply; not re-read for Christmas Island today. Christmas Island follows Australia: the ITAA 1997 takes 'Australia' in a geographical sense to include the Territory of Christmas Island (s 960-505, read today in the 1 October 2026 compilation), and Commonwealth law applies there unless excluded (Acts Interpretation Act 1901, as producer-CX.json holds from ALRC Report 80), the Fair Work Act included. This item is Australia's, as the first wave recorded it in t4.result.json (AU); its sources were read there on 2026-11-04 and are not re-fetched here. AU's note: A series is a film under s376-20; drama series have no 65-hour limit. Significant Australian content (s376-70) is a further test not read here.

sources.said: For episodic or feature length projects for which Television (including SVOD or BVOD) is the first and primary window, applicants must: o have a local commissioning platform secured on terms acceptable to Screen Australia, including meeting the following minimum licence fee requirements*, … a confirmed minimum licence fee of $550,000 per broadcast hour allocated toward the initial licence period (3 years) against the primary right … for Children’s content, a confirmed minimum of: • $125,000 per broadcast half hour for one commissioning platform with limited exclusivity holdbacks; or • $144,000 for (i) combination of commissioning platforms; or (ii) one commissioning platform with full exclusivity … o have secured a ROW Distributor with a letter of offer (LOO) … the first funding decision within the updated minimum licence fee requirements being in force from 1 July 2026
